summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, congestive heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, diabetes, morbid obesity, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for left leg swelling present for two weeks. Evaluation revealed chronic venous insufficiency with early skin breakdown and signs of cellulitis, but no deep vein thrombosis on ultrasound. She was afebrile with stable vital signs and no evidence of acute heart failure, supported by low BNP and mild imaging changes. She was treated with antibiotics for cellulitis and advised to resume daily diuretic use. Compression therapy was recommended for venous insufficiency, and anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation was deferred pending cardiology follow-up. She improved clinically and was discharged to extended care with outpatient follow-up plans.
